title: Laws of Motion

notes.heading: 1. Newton's Laws, Impulse & Linear Momentum Conservation
notes.proseLatex: Newton's second law in general form is $\vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt} = m\vec{a} + \vec{v}_{\text{rel}}\frac{dm}{dt}$ where $\vec{p} = m\vec{v}$. Impulse $\vec{J} = \int \vec{F}\,dt = \Delta\vec{p}$ equals the area under the $F$-$t$ graph. When $\vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}$ (explosions, gun recoil, collisions), total system momentum $\sum m_i \vec{v}_i$ stays strictly conserved regardless of internal inelastic losses. Action-reaction pairs ($\vec{F}_{AB} = -\vec{F}_{BA}$) ALWAYS act on two DIFFERENT bodies, so they never cancel on a single free-body diagram.

keyFormulas.label: Impulse-Momentum & Apparent Weight in Lift
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Compute impulse from F-t graphs and apparent normal force inside accelerating frames.

examples.problemLatex: Two masses $m_1 = 3\text{ kg}$ and $m_2 = 5\text{ kg}$ hang over a light frictionless Atwood pulley ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$). Find acceleration $a$ and string tension $T$.

notes.heading: 2. Static vs Kinetic Friction, Angle of Repose & Pulling vs Pushing
notes.proseLatex: Static friction is SELF-ADJUSTING up to its limiting ceiling $0 \le f_s \le \mu_s N$ ($f_s$ equals applied tangential load until slip begins!), whereas kinetic friction once sliding is $f_k = \mu_k N$ ($\mu_k < \mu_s$). Angle of friction $\lambda = \arctan\mu_s$ equals the angle of repose $\theta_r$ on an inclined plane. Pulling a lawn-roller at angle $\theta$ reduces $N = mg - F\sin\theta$ and requires less force than pushing ($N = mg + F\sin\theta$).

keyFormulas.label: Self-Adjusting Static Friction & Angle of Repose
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Avoid plugging mu_s*N blindly when block remains at rest.

examples.problemLatex: A $10\text{ kg}$ block rests on a horizontal floor ($\mu_s = 0.5, \mu_k = 0.4, g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$). What friction force acts when a horizontal pull of $32\text{ N}$ is applied?
stepsLatex: Since $F = 32\text{ N} < 50\text{ N}$, the block stays at rest and self-adjusting static friction equals $32\text{ N}$ (NOT $50\text{ N}$!).

notes.heading: 3. Circular Dynamics & Road Banking
notes.proseLatex: Centripetal force $mv^2/r$ is NOT an extra physical interaction — it is the net inward resultant of tension, normal reaction, gravity, or friction. On a flat unbanked turn, $v_{\max} = \sqrt{\mu_s r g}$; on a frictionless banked curve at angle $\theta$, optimum no-wear speed satisfies $\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{rg}$, and with banking plus friction, $v_{\max} = \sqrt{rg\,\frac{\tan\theta + \mu_s}{1 - \mu_s\tan\theta}}$.

keyFormulas.label: Unbanked & Banked Curve Safe Speeds
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Compute safe cornering speeds and optimum banking angles.

wbjeebTraps: Static friction trap: if $F_{\text{applied}} < \mu_s N$, friction equals $F_{\text{applied}}$, NEVER $\mu_s N$!
Normal force $N$ does NOT equal $mg$ on inclines ($N = mg\cos\theta$), in accelerating lifts, or under oblique pulls ($N = mg \mp F\sin\theta$).
In an inertial frame, never draw both an outward 'centrifugal force' AND set $\sum F_{\text{in}} = mv^2/r$ — pick EITHER inertial FBD OR rotating frame with pseudo-force, never both.

conceptPrimer.heading: Newton's Second Law, Impulse & Momentum Conservation
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $\vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt}$ with $\vec{p} = m\vec{v}$; impulse $\vec{J} = \int\vec{F}\,dt = \Delta\vec{p}$ = area under $F$-$t$. With $\vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}$ (explosions, recoil, collisions) total momentum is conserved regardless of energy losses. Micro-check: $10\,\text{g}$ bullet at $400\,\text{m/s}$ from a $4\,\text{kg}$ rifle: recoil $= \frac{0.01\times400}{4} = 1\,\text{m/s}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Action-Reaction Pairs Act on Different Bodies
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $\vec{F}_{AB} = -\vec{F}_{BA}$ act on TWO different bodies, so they never cancel within one free-body diagram — the horse-cart paradox dissolves on the horse's FBD. Micro-check: book on table: the table pushes the book up; the book pushes the table down — different bodies.

conceptPrimer.heading: Static vs Kinetic Friction & Angle of Repose
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Static friction is self-adjusting: $0 \le f_s \le \mu_s N$ — it equals the applied load until slip starts, NEVER $\mu_s N$ prematurely. Once sliding: $f_k = \mu_k N$ with $\mu_k < \mu_s$. Angle of friction $\lambda = \tan^{-1}\mu_s$ equals the angle of repose $\theta_r$. Micro-check: $F = 3\,\text{N} < \mu_s N = 5\,\text{N}$: friction $= 3\,\text{N}$, block static.

conceptPrimer.heading: Normal Force Is NOT Always $mg$
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: On an incline $N = mg\cos\theta$; in a lift accelerating up $N = m(g + a)$; under a pull at angle $\theta$ above horizontal $N = mg - F\sin\theta$ (pushing: $mg + F\sin\theta$) — so PULLING a roller is easier than pushing. Micro-check: $F = 20\,\text{N}$ at $30°$ on $10\,\text{kg}$: $N = 100 - 10 = 90\,\text{N}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Centripetal Force Is a Resultant, Not a New Force
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $mv^2/r$ is the net inward component of real forces (tension, normal, gravity, friction) — never draw it as an extra arrow. Flat turn: $v_{\max} = \sqrt{\mu_s rg}$. Banked curve (frictionless): $\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{rg}$; with friction $v_{\max} = \sqrt{rg\frac{\tan\theta + \mu_s}{1 - \mu_s\tan\theta}}$. Micro-check: $\mu = 0.5$, $r = 20$, $g = 10$: $v_{\max} = 10\,\text{m/s}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Inertial vs Rotating Frames: Pick One
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: In an inertial frame, set $\sum F_{\text{inward}} = \frac{mv^2}{r}$ with real forces only. In a rotating frame you may add a centrifugal pseudo-force — but never both at once (double counting). Micro-check: conical pendulum: inertial route gives $\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{rg}$ with $T\cos\theta = mg$.

memoryHooks: No external force $\Rightarrow$ momentum conserved (even inelastic).
Third-law pairs: different bodies, never cancel on one FBD.
Static friction matches the push until slip; ceiling $\mu_s N$.
Pick inertial FBD or rotating frame — one only.
commonMistakes: Drawing $N = mg$ on inclines or in lifts.
Cancelling action-reaction pairs on one body's diagram.
Forgetting $F\sin\theta$ in the normal for oblique pushes/pulls.
Treating centripetal force as a physical interaction.
Rushing the final unit conversion after a correct setup.
examChecklist: Impulse-momentum for variable-force and collision questions.
Conserve momentum in isolated explosions (regardless of $e$).
Apply the static-friction window before slip.
Compute $N$ for inclines, lifts, oblique forces.
Flat/banked turn speed limits with and without friction.
Keep third-law pairs off a single FBD.
Choose inertial or rotating frame consistently.
